tasks.short: Assess incoming material, decide its significance and arrange appropriate distribution.

steps.what: Collect incoming memos, submissions and reports.
Read documents and identify requests, deadlines and relevant background.

loop.input: Accessible incoming material and its document metadata.
loop.output: A brief containing requests, deadlines, named parties and source passages.
loop.check: Require a source passage for each finding; flag missing dates and conflicting statements.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unreadable or unsupported items return to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests and deadlines appear in varied prose and document layouts.

steps.what: Judge significance, sensitivity and the need for executive attention.
Select recipients and specify the action expected from each.
Forward material and record its distribution.

tasks.design: Configure the {EMAIL} review queue and use a bounded extraction step to create source-linked briefs in the {DOCS}. The assistant judges significance, approves recipients in the {WORKFLOW}, and releases permission-checked internal distribution through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Routing depends on executive context, confidentiality and informal relationships. Earlier rules could sort senders but could not reliably interpret varied documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing queue rules handle collection and delivery. Bounded extraction can prepare traceable briefs, while AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records and permissions.
tasks.still_hard: Political significance, implied urgency and permission boundaries remain difficult. A correct summary can still miss why an issue matters.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant understands competing priorities, notices sensitive implications and knows when private escalation is better than wider circulation.

ambition.what: A daily executive attention brief with explicit escalation decisions.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from reading every page and forwarding attachments toward assessing competing issues and checking follow-through. Formal decision rights do not change; escalation authority remains delegated by the executive.

reach.task: Prepare issue briefs that compare implications across departments.
reach.learn: Problem framing, evidence quality and how to distinguish a signal from background detail.

evidence.claim: Queue rules and permission-aware distribution can automate collection and delivery; contextual significance remains human judgement.
The Department for Business and Trade evaluation observed hallucinations and found no evidence of higher productivity; local validation is necessary.
Step shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates rather than measured outcomes.

assumptions: The representative workflow distributes material internally; external disclosure requires separate authority.
Time shares describe a typical task instance, not a measured customer baseline.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot using existing systems and exclude waiting for procurement or consultation decisions.
GDPR access limits, purpose limitation and retention apply to the brief as well as the original material.
unknowns: Which executive priorities and escalation thresholds the assistant may apply independently.
Whether document permissions can be checked before distribution.
The volume of scanned files, restricted attachments and exceptional recipient lists.
Applicable national consultation requirements and existing employee agreements.
research_questions: Does source-linked extraction reduce reading time without missing significant issues?
Can existing queue and permission features support the pilot without custom integration?
new_work: Check unsupported findings and conflicting deadlines.
Maintain distribution groups, access rules and escalation criteria.
Sample briefs for missed context and inappropriate recipient suggestions.
Monitor connector failures and document retention.

tasks.short: Handle administrative requests for other departments, including documents, record updates and routine correspondence.

steps.what: Read departmental requests and identify the requested administrative output.

loop.input: A support request and an approved catalogue of request types.
loop.output: A draft request record containing output type, requester, deadline and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate against the catalogue and required fields; retain the source request beside extracted values.
loop.stop: One extraction attempt; ambiguous or unsupported requests enter the clarification queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Existing requests arrive as varied free text. A configured form handles new structured submissions.

steps.what: Clarify scope, urgency and missing information with the requesting department.
Find current records, approved templates and supporting information.
Prepare the requested document or routine correspondence from approved information.
Check departmental facts and approve the output.
Return the approved output and confirm completion.

tasks.design: Configure a request register in the {WORKFLOW}, with structured forms and bounded extraction for requests arriving through the {EMAIL}. Deterministic lookups assemble permitted records from the {DOCS}, and template generators prepare standard outputs for departmental approval before delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests mixed missing information, informal priorities and many document variants. A shared mailbox provided flexibility but little reusable structure.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, approval flows and template generation already cover much of the work. Small integrations and bounded request extraction make the remaining gaps cheaper to address.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual requests need negotiation and bespoke work. Departmental record quality and template ownership limit reuse.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant understands what colleagues actually need, negotiates realistic deadlines and handles requests that do not fit a standard service.

ambition.what: A weekly decision on which cross-department request bottleneck to remove.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward resolving incomplete requests and improving recurring administrative services. With delegation, the assistant can sequence standard requests within agreed service levels; departmental content approval stays with the department.

reach.task: Triage a shared request backlog and identify blocked dependencies.
reach.learn: Capacity planning, dependency mapping and practical service-level measures.

evidence.claim: Forms, record lookups, templates and approval flows suit repeatable clerical requests without autonomous agents.
The Department for Business and Trade evaluation reported drafting time savings, but these do not establish gains for this mixed clerical workload.
Step shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates for a limited request catalogue.

assumptions: The steps represent common document and correspondence requests; specialist transactions require their own departmental workflow.
The pilot starts with a few recurring request types and approved templates.
Outputs are delivered internally; external commitments require the relevant delegated authority.
GDPR applies to personal information in requests and source records.
Build ranges cover working effort; national consultation and access decisions may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: The most frequent request types and their actual time distribution.
Which departments maintain authoritative records and current templates.
The assistant's authority to prioritise requests or update departmental records.
Whether proposed queue reporting would monitor individual employees and trigger national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which request types can use structured forms and templates without losing necessary flexibility?
Does clarification effort fall after introducing required fields?
If staff allocation or monitoring is added, does the intended use fall within EU AI Act Annex III?
new_work: Resolve ambiguous requests and unsupported request types.
Maintain forms, templates, lookup mappings and service definitions.
Check that source access remains limited to the requesting department's needs.
Review bottlenecks without turning service reporting into unnecessary employee monitoring.

tasks.short: Attend meetings, draft accurate minutes and arrange their approval, circulation and filing.

steps.what: Review the agenda, meeting papers and previous minutes.
Attend the meeting and capture notes using conferencing software.
Turn meeting notes into minutes containing decisions, actions and owners.

loop.input: An authorised meeting transcript or human notes, agenda and meeting papers.
loop.output: Draft minutes with source-linked decisions, actions, owners and explicitly stated deadlines.
loop.check: Trace decisions to source passages; flag disputed wording, uncertain speakers and missing owners without inventing them.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision after review; unresolved decisions return to the assistant and chair.
loop.why_not_simpler: Discussion is unstructured, and a template cannot distinguish proposals from agreed decisions.

steps.what: Resolve disputed wording and approve the official minutes.
Circulate approved minutes to the authorised attendee list.
File the approved version with the meeting records.

tasks.design: Generate an agenda-based template from the {DOCS} and configure authorised transcription in the conferencing software represented by {OTHER}. A bounded drafting step prepares source-linked minutes for assistant review and chair approval; the {WORKFLOW} then controls circulation through the {EMAIL} and filing in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Capturing discussion and distinguishing decisions from debate required sustained attention. Earlier transcription alone left substantial drafting and checking work.
tasks.enabler_now: Meeting transcription and draft-note features already exist. Bounded drafting can follow a fixed minutes structure, with ordinary approval and retention controls around it.
tasks.still_hard: Sensitive meetings may prohibit recording or require full human attendance. Overlapping speech, implied agreement and formal approval requirements still demand judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant notices unresolved disagreement, asks for a clear decision and preserves an accurate record without flattening sensitive discussion.

ambition.what: A searchable decision history for recurring leadership meetings.

tasks.altitude: For routine recordable meetings, the assistant spends less time transcribing and more time confirming decisions and following up unclear actions. The chair retains approval authority; the assistant gains no new formal decision rights.

reach.task: Track meeting actions through to evidenced completion.
reach.learn: Action ownership, dependency tracking and clear completion criteria.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Teams Facilitator provides live meeting notes, supporting configured capture rather than bespoke transcription development.
iBabs Debrief provides transcripts, summaries and board-meeting minutes; this establishes capability, not local accuracy or savings.
The Department for Business and Trade evaluation reported meeting-summary time savings and observed hallucinations.
In the Netherlands, works-council consent requirements can apply to employee-data and monitoring arrangements introduced with transcription.
AI literacy requirements apply; ordinary minutes drafting is not itself an Annex III employment use.
The proposed remaining effort and build ranges are estimates for routine, authorised, recordable meetings.

assumptions: The reduced capture time assumes the assistant need not attend every minute solely to take notes.
Meetings requiring full attendance or prohibiting recording retain more manual work.
The chair can approve minutes under the meeting's governance rules; some bodies require wider approval.
Recording requires an appropriate GDPR basis, participant information, controlled access and defined retention; a chair's approval alone is insufficient.
Consent and access ranges cover working effort, including consultation preparation; elapsed consultation time may be longer.
unknowns: Which meetings permit recording and which require full assistant attendance.
Applicable national consultation rules and existing recording agreements.
Whether a DPIA is required for the proposed processing.
Required languages, audio quality, approval rules and retention periods.
Whether the attendee list includes external participants requiring separate distribution controls.
research_questions: How often do draft minutes confuse a proposal with an agreed decision?
Does capture review plus editing save time for each meeting type?
Can existing document metadata support a searchable decision history without another repository?
new_work: Check uncertain speakers, decisions, owners and deadlines against source material.
Resolve corrections with the chair before publication.
Maintain recording permissions, participant information and deletion schedules.
Test minute quality across languages, accents and meeting formats.
Maintain the approved decision index and remove superseded drafts.

tasks.short: Collect, validate and submit approved employee changes and time information for payroll processing.

steps.what: Retrieve approved employee changes, absence records and time information.
Request missing submissions and approvals before the payroll cutoff.
Resolve disputed or incomplete submissions with the responsible manager.
Combine approved inputs into the monthly payroll worksheet.
Enter or upload payroll inputs into the payroll system.
Reconcile input totals and investigate validation errors or unexpected changes.
Approve the reconciled payroll input batch for processing.

tasks.design: Configure cutoff reminders and approved input exports from the {HCM}, then map those records directly into a staged batch in the {PAYROLL}. Deterministic checks reconcile identifiers, effective dates, duplicates and control totals; the assistant resolves exceptions and the payroll lead approves processing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different identifiers, effective-date rules and approval formats made copying into a worksheet convenient. Reliable integration also required access and agreement on authoritative records.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing export and import functions support structured transfer. Small deterministic mappings and reconciliation checks can be built and maintained with less coding effort.
tasks.still_hard: Retroactive changes, disputed hours and national payroll rules require payroll expertise. An interface must distinguish staging from processing and prevent duplicate submissions.
tasks.human_edge: People resolve disputed entitlements, understand unusual employment circumstances and take responsibility for payroll approval.

ambition.what: A weekly decision on unresolved payroll-input exceptions before cutoff.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time consolidating and retyping data and more time resolving missing approvals before cutoff. Payroll calculation, entitlement interpretation and payment authority remain with authorised payroll and finance roles; no new formal rights are assumed.

reach.learn: Payroll cutoffs, effective dates, reconciliation controls and separation of duties.

evidence.claim: Structured payroll inputs suit configured exports, deterministic mappings and reconciliation rather than model interpretation.
Staging, duplicate prevention, control totals and approval separation are established integration controls.
The digest provides no documented payroll implementation or measured payroll saving; effort and build ranges are estimates.

assumptions: The assistant prepares payroll inputs rather than calculating pay, filing returns or releasing bank payments.
A worksheet commonly bridges approved records and payroll import in this representative workflow.
Only approved changes are transferred; entitlement decisions are not inferred from free text.
The target interface supports staging without triggering a pay run.
The pilot covers one payroll population and includes parallel reconciliation across payroll cycles.
GDPR requires restricted access and data minimisation; national employment and consultation rules vary.
Build ranges describe working effort; payroll-cycle timing and consultation may extend elapsed rollout.
unknowns: Whether the existing systems already provide a supported connection that only needs configuration.
The actual source of time records and the assistant's permitted payroll access.
Employee identifier mappings, pay codes and retroactive-change rules.
Whether uploads stage inputs or immediately affect processing.
Existing approval roles, payroll calendars and national requirements.
Whether employee or works-council consultation is required for the proposed change.
research_questions: Can native integration eliminate the worksheet without custom code?
Can imports be retried without creating duplicate payroll changes?
Which reconciliation checks detect materially wrong inputs before approval?
new_work: Investigate failed mappings, missing approvals and unexpected variances.
Maintain pay-code mappings, cutoff calendars and effective-date rules.
Reconcile transferred records after interface or payroll configuration changes.
Review access logs and remove unnecessary payroll-data copies.
Retest duplicate prevention and staging behaviour after system updates.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward protecting executive attention, clarifying requests, confirming meeting decisions and resolving administrative exceptions. Formal authority remains delegated; broader coordination rights need explicit agreement.
reach: Management analyst: prepare evidence-based issue briefs across departments.
Project management specialist: track administrative dependencies and meeting actions.
Administrative services manager: coordinate shared service capacity and payroll-input readiness.
skills_to_grow: Source checking and concise issue briefing.
Request design, template maintenance and workflow configuration.
Permission management, GDPR basics and appropriate AI use.
Reconciliation, exception analysis and effective-date handling.
role.ambitious_version: An executive operations coordinator who provides a daily attention brief, a trusted decision history and early warning of cross-department administrative bottlenecks.

job.title: Executive Secretaries and Executive Administrative Assistants
